records.name: Taiwan
records.summary:
Taiwan is a progressive Asian destination — it was the first in Asia to legalise same-sex marriage (2019), the government is investing US$8.76 million to double gender-neutral public bathrooms by 2029, and a trans march in Taipei drew 3,000 participants in 2025. There are no documented severe incidents (no mob violence, trans-tourist rape, or organised dating-app predation).

The main gaps are legal-gender-recognition reform stagnation — a 2008 Ministry order still requires sex-reassignment surgery to change one's gender marker (blocking an estimated 90% of trans people, with only case-by-case court exceptions), and the government has been "floundering" on reform — and a rising anti-gender discourse movement that has produced online waves of hostility. A trans woman was outed during a police identity inspection (the Viva case), and Taipei has held a vigil for victims of anti-trans violence.

For a visitor, bathrooms are unrestricted (and being proactively expanded to gender-neutral), there is no criminalisation, and border/immigration poses no trans-specific friction. Taipei City has trans-friendly service guidelines.

records.name: Mississippi
records.summary:
Mississippi enacted public-facility bans in 2024 and 2025 and defines legal sex by birth in statute, placing it in the worst-law group of the July 2026 per-state legal-risk grading.

One institutional counterweight is documented: a federal court sentenced the killer of a trans woman in Lucedale to 49 years for a bias-motivated murder — evidence that violence here can meet real prosecutorial response even while hostile law stands.

records.name: Oklahoma
records.summary:
Oklahoma enacted facility bans in 2022 and 2025 and defines legal sex by birth in statute.

The July 2026 per-state legal-risk assessment lists it among the worst states for legislation targeting transgender adults.

records.name: Indiana
records.summary: A February 2026 per-state legal-risk assessment placed Indiana 'among the harshest anti-trans states in the country', citing its 2026 identity-document law and escalating bathroom restrictions as the drivers of its adult-risk rating; the July 2026 edition keeps it in the worst-state group.

records.name: Utah
records.summary:
Utah's HB 257 (January 2024) was the first statewide bathroom ban in the country reaching trans adults, not only school facilities; it remains in force, alongside birth-certificate and surgery requirements for amended markers and a complaint channel for objecting officials.

In May 2025 Utah became the first state to explicitly prohibit flying LGBTQ flags at government buildings and schools (fines up to $500 per day), with similar flag bans following in other states — its Pride organisation calls the state's legislative record the nation's most anti-LGBT.
